newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian lawmaker attacked by settlers.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian lawmaker attacked by settlers.

text.p: A Palestinian lawmaker said extremist Jewish settlers attacked him in Jerusalem on Wednesday and damaged his car, demanding he leave the city.

"Five settlers belonging to the extremist Ideological Front followed my car in Jerusalem and when I stopped at the traffic lights, they attacked me and destroyed parts of my car," said Abbas Zaki, a member of the Palestinian Legislative Council.

"They cursed me and called Palestinians dogs and shouted at us to leave Jerusalem and said they will haunt us and will prevent Palestinian officials from entering Jerusalem," Zaki told Reuters. He said he was not badly hurt.
Noam Federman, spokesman for the Ideological Front, an offshoot of the outlawed extremist Jewish organisation Kach, confirmed that members of the Front attacked Zaki.

"Yes, they attacked him after they went after him and they saw it was Zaki, the senior terrorist of the PLO," Federman said. "Every time we catch people from the PLO, they will get the same treatment," he added.
Israeli police said they were investigating the incident.
Palestinian officials and lawmakers, who carry VIP cards enabling them to travel freely in Israel, have recently complained of harassment by Israeli soldiers at checkpoints and by settlers.
They say relations between Palestinians and Israelis have deteriorated since the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu came to power last year.
Lawmaker Jamal al-Shobaki said on Tuesday that the Israeli army detained him and three of his colleagues inside a military base near the West Bank city of Ramallah for four and a half hours.
